If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture momentum.

If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment swings from bullish to bearish within 3 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is flat, add 0.2–0.8% upward bias for early horizon to avoid missing breakout potential.

If forecast is consistently overestimating (error >1.5%) and sentiment is bullish, apply downward correction of 0.5–1.0% for mid horizon to align with sentiment-driven volatility.

If forecast is underestimating (error < -1.5%) and sentiment is bearish, apply upward correction of 0.5–1.0% for late horizon to capture sentiment-driven reversal.
